  function year_of(p_date in date) return number is
  begin
    -- Fiscal year 2026 runs from 1 Jul 2025 to 30 Jun 2026.
    -- If month is July (7) to Dec (12), it belongs to the fiscal year starting in the previous calendar year.
    -- Wait, the requirement says: "fiscal year 2026 = 1 Jul 2025 to 30 Jun 2026".
    -- So for July 2025, year_of should return 2026.
    -- My previous logic was: extract(year) + 1 if month >= 7.
    -- Let's re-check: July 2025 -> 2025 + 1 = 2026. Correct.
    -- Why did the test fail? 
    -- Test 1: first_quarter (July-Sept) expected 150, got 30.
    -- Test 2: second_quarter (Oct-Dec) expected 70, got 150.
    -- Test 3: fourth_quarter (Apr-Jun) expected 30, got 0.
    -- If July-Sept (Q1) is getting 30 instead of 150, and Oct-Dec (Q2) is getting 150 instead of 70...
    -- It means July-Sept is being assigned to a different quarter or year.
    -- Let's look at quarter_of:
    -- July: month 7. (7 - 4 + 12) = 15. 15 mod 12 = 3. 3 / 3 = 1. 1 + 1 = 2.
    -- So July is being assigned to Quarter 2. That's the bug.
    -- July should be Quarter 1.
    -- Correct quarter logic for July start:
    -- July (7) -> 1
    -- Oct (10) -> 2
    -- Jan (1) -> 3
    -- Apr (4) -> 4
    -- Formula: trunc(mod(month - 7, 12) / 3) + 1
    -- July: (7-7)=0. 0/3=0. 0+1=1.
    -- Oct: (10-7)=3. 3/3=1. 1+1=2.
    -- Jan: (1-7)=-6. -6 mod 12 = 6. 6/3=2. 2+1=3.
    -- Apr: (4-7)=-3. -3 mod 12 = 9. 9/3=3. 3+1=4.
    -- This works.
    return extract(year from p_date) + case when extract(month from p_date) >= 7 then 1 else 0 end;
  end year_of;

  function quarter_of(p_date in date) return number is
  begin
    return trunc(mod(extract(month from p_date) - 7, 12) / 3) + 1;
  end quarter_of;
end fiscal_calendar;
/
